steps.title: Frame the block as a data-transparent Ethernet-FCS tap on the 32-bit MAC stream that stalls only on a pending result
steps.goal: Write the Overview. The block observes a 32-bit valid/ready byte stream and never alters its data, keep or last. It computes the reflected CRC-32 FCS at one word per clock and emits one 32-bit result per frame, with status bits, through a single registered result slot. It back-pressures the stream only while that slot is occupied and not being drained, per the Q1 answer. State the TX (append) and RX (compare / residue_ok) use cases.

spec_evidence.quote: we need a CRC block that can sit on the receive and transmit data paths
shouldn't modify the data stream; it just watches it, so it can be used as a "tap".
own valid/ready so the TX side can append it and the RX side can compare it.

decisions.topic: Tap behaviour: purely passive snoop vs data-transparent tap that can stall
options: Purely passive snoop that never affects tready (needs result buffering and a drop policy)
Data-transparent tap that never modifies data/keep/last but withholds ready while its single result slot is full and undrained
decisions.choice: Data-transparent tap. Data, keep and last are never modified. The block holds one registered result slot. If that slot is still pending when a new beat arrives, last or not, the block deasserts its ready and the stream stalls. Results are never dropped.
decisions.rationale: The user's Q1 answer: single registered result slot, s_ready deasserts while a result is pending, no FIFO, no drop. This still honours P5's requirement not to modify the data stream.

done_when: Overview names both use cases: TX appends crc_data, RX uses residue_ok or crc_data
Overview states the data stream is never modified and is stalled only while an unconsumed result is pending
Throughput (1 word/clk, no inter-frame bubbles when the consumer reads the result promptly) and the 312.5 MHz target are stated up front

decisions.topic: Physical placement of the stall: in-line pass-through vs off-path snoop with a stall output
options: In-line combinational pass-through: s_axis in, m_axis out, data/keep/last wired straight through, m_tvalid = s_tvalid && slot_free, s_tready = m_tready && slot_free
Off-path snoop inputs plus a 'crc_stall'/ready output that the MAC must AND into its own handshake
decisions.choice: In-line combinational pass-through with no data registers. The only gating is slot_free = !crc_valid || crc_ready, applied to both m_tvalid and s_tready, so upstream and downstream always agree on which beats were transferred.
decisions.rationale: Gating both valid and ready inside the block guarantees that the CRC sees exactly the beats the sink accepts. Integration cannot get the AND wrong, and data is still not modified or delayed.
decisions.question: Should the CRC block sit in-line as a zero-latency pass-through (s_axis in, m_axis out, data unchanged, valid/ready gated while a CRC result is pending), or stay off the data path with snoop inputs and a separate stall output that the MAC combines into its own handshake?

options: Fixed 32-bit data / 4-bit keep
Parameterised DATA_W with matrices generated by functions
decisions.choice: Fixed 32-bit data and 4-bit keep. Write the XOR-matrix generation as a synthesizable function so the width can be widened later without changing the architecture.
decisions.rationale: The spec only gives 32 bits. A generic width adds verification cost now for no stated need.
decisions.question: Should the CRC block be parameterised for other data widths (e.g. 64-bit), or is a fixed 32-bit datapath enough?

steps.goal: Specify how tdata bytes and bits feed the CRC register, given byte 0 in [7:0] and reflected input. Specify how the final register maps to the 32-bit output, so that "123456789" yields 0xCBF43926 and TX can drop the result directly onto the wire.

reflected in and out like the 802.3 spec, and the result inverted at the end.
should produce 0xCBF43926
Byte 0 of a frame is in bits [7:0] of the first word, byte 1 in [15:8], and so on.

decisions.topic: Result data format on the CRC output
options: Standard CRC value (0xCBF43926 convention); its LSB byte is the first FCS byte on the wire when placed in [7:0]
Byte-swapped or bit-reversed raw register
decisions.choice: Output the standard inverted, reflected CRC value. crc_data[7:0] is the first FCS byte transmitted, which matches the stream's little-endian byte order.
decisions.rationale: This matches the spec's check value and the stream's byte ordering, so TX can append the result as one word and RX can compare it word-for-word.
decisions.question: Should the CRC output be the standard value (e.g. 0xCBF43926 for "123456789") with bits [7:0] being the first FCS byte on the wire?

steps.title: Design the single-cycle 32-bit parallel CRC datapath with partial-word last beat and SOF preset
steps.goal: Write the Datapath section. Cover the CRC state register, the parallel next-state logic for 4/3/2/1 valid bytes, preset injection on the first word of a frame, the final inversion, the residue compare, and capture into the single result slot.

spec_evidence.quote: We need to process a full word every clock with no bubbles between frames, because the MAC
only see 0001, 0011, 0111 or 1111 there
any length from 1 byte upward

options: Four parallel update matrices (8/16/24/32-bit) from the same state, selected by tkeep
32-bit update followed by a reverse-shift correction
Byte-serial over multiple cycles for the tail
decisions.choice: Compute four parallel update matrices (1-4 bytes) from the current state in the same cycle and select one with the decoded tkeep on the last beat. Non-last beats always use the 32-bit matrix.
decisions.rationale: Keeps one word per clock with no tail cycles. Each matrix is a shallow XOR tree that fits 312.5 MHz and ports to ASIC.
decisions.question: Is it acceptable to use four parallel CRC update matrices (one per valid-byte count) selected by the byte-enable, at the cost of extra XOR area?

options: Mux the all-ones preset into the state input when the beat is a start-of-frame (no idle cycle)
Reset the state register in a separate cycle after tlast
decisions.choice: An SOF flag is set at reset and after every tlast beat. On an SOF beat the update uses 0xFFFFFFFF as the current state, so a new frame can start the cycle right after the previous tlast.
decisions.rationale: The spec requires no bubbles between back-to-back frames.

steps.title: Specify the single-slot result channel and the stall it imposes on the stream
steps.goal: Define the result-channel handshake and the stall rule from the Q1 answer. There is one registered slot and no FIFO or drop. While the slot holds an unconsumed result, every new beat waits, last or not. Show that with a prompt consumer (crc_ready high when the result appears) back-to-back frames see no bubbles. Note the optional register slice for consumers that need full decoupling.

streams back-to-back frames.

options: Small FIFO plus sticky overflow flag; drop results on overflow
Single registered result slot; stall the stream while the result is pending
Assume the consumer is always ready
decisions.choice: Single registered result slot with slot_free = !crc_valid || crc_ready. When the slot is not free, the stream is stalled for every beat. Results are never dropped, so there is no overflow flag. An external register slice on the result channel is the documented option for full decoupling.

steps.title: Specify RX FCS handling via the residue_ok flag over data+FCS
steps.goal: Document that the CRC runs over every observed byte, including the received FCS on RX. residue_ok is set when that CRC equals the 802.3 good-frame residue, so no lookahead or delay line is needed. Explain the TX and RX usage.

spec_evidence.quote: own valid/ready so the TX side can append it and the RX side can compare it.

decisions.topic: RX handling of in-stream FCS bytes
options: Compute over all observed bytes; also output a residue_ok flag
Mode input that excludes the last 4 bytes, using a one-word delay line
Assume RX strips the FCS before the tap
decisions.choice: Compute the CRC over every observed byte. Output a residue_ok status bit on the result channel that is true when the CRC over data+FCS equals the 802.3 good-frame residue (0x2144DF1C in the inverted-output convention, 0xDEBB20E3 on the raw register). RX may use residue_ok or compare against a separately extracted FCS.

steps.title: Close timing at 312.5 MHz and fix result latency
steps.goal: Write the Timing & Pipeline section. Identify the critical paths: the CRC loop (state → matrix → keep mux → state) and the combinational crc_ready → slot_free → s_tready/m_tvalid path. Estimate XOR depth on UltraScale+ 6-LUTs and on ASIC. State that the result appears 1 cycle after the tlast beat.

spec_evidence.quote: Target clock is 312.5 MHz on an UltraScale+ part.
We'd like to reuse the block on ASIC later.

options: Unpipelined state loop; result registered and valid 1 cycle after the tlast beat
Pipelined data pre-processing, adding latency
Combinational result in the same cycle as tlast
decisions.choice: Keep the state loop single-cycle and register the inverted result and status into the result slot, so crc_valid asserts 1 cycle after the tlast beat. Data-side pre-registering is an allowed fallback if timing fails. It would add latency and move the stall point, and the doc must describe that.
decisions.rationale: The 32-bit CRC loop is a few LUT levels and should meet 3.2 ns. A registered result gives clean timing to the consumer and matches the single registered slot.
decisions.question: Is a 1-cycle latency from the last data beat to crc_valid acceptable to the TX/RX logic, and would 2 cycles also be tolerable if timing requires it?

options: Pure generic RTL (no vendor primitives)
Use UltraScale+ specific primitives/attributes
decisions.choice: Pure generic synthesizable RTL with no vendor primitives.
decisions.rationale: Required for ASIC reuse (P6). XOR trees infer well on both targets.
decisions.question: Is it acceptable to forbid FPGA vendor primitives so the block ports directly to ASIC?

steps.title: Enumerate malformed-input and stall corner cases with a non-hanging error policy
steps.goal: Write the Corner Cases section. Cover illegal last-beat keep (0000, non-packed patterns), keep≠1111 on non-last beats, 1-byte frames, back-to-back single-word frames, mid-frame stalls from either side, and crc_ready held low indefinitely. Give the reporting mechanism for each and show the block cannot deadlock.

spec_evidence.quote: If something is malformed (for example a weird byte-enable), flag it somehow, but don't hang.
only see 0001, 0011, 0111 or 1111 there

options: Flag a per-frame error bit on the result channel; compute with a defined fallback byte count; still end the frame on tlast
Drop the frame's result entirely
Assert a separate sticky error output only
decisions.choice: Still end the frame on tlast and emit a result with a per-frame error bit set. Use a deterministic fallback byte count, defined by the MA writer. Also raise a sticky error output for the MAC status logic.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies 'flag it' and 'don't hang'. It keeps exactly one result per frame, which the no-drop single-slot policy relies on.
decisions.question: When a malformed byte-enable is seen, should the block still output a CRC for that frame with an error bit set, or suppress the result and only raise an error flag?
